brief: A recipe manager as a transformation timeline — ingredients flow through steps and combine into the dish

dominant_strengths: Strong conceptual metaphor: ingredients literally flow through transformation nodes into the final dish, making process legible at a glance
Clear three-pane information architecture with disciplined typographic hierarchy across collection, canvas, and detail
Color-coded node stages (green inputs, blue actions, purple combinations, red result) reinforce the timeline narrative semantically
dominant_weaknesses: Saturated primary palette (kindergarten green/blue/purple/red) clashes with the refined orange accent system used in the side panels
Connector lines are thin gray and orthogonal but lack arrowheads or directional cues, weakening the 'flow' the brief promises
Heavy redundancy: ingredients appear in green nodes AND the right rail, with no progressive disclosure or interactive payoff
fix_priorities: Desaturate node fills to a tonal palette tied to the orange brand, reserving color for stage semantics not decoration
Add directional flow affordances — animated dots, arrowheads, or progressive reveal — to make the timeline feel alive
Resolve ingredient duplication by making nodes the canonical source and collapsing the right rail into steps + meta only
Introduce a temporal axis or time-scrubber so the 'transformation timeline' is navigable, not just a static diagram
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral and reflective lead through clear process logic, but visceral appeal is dampened by the loud, mismatched node palette.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — the node graph genuinely expresses ingredient-to-dish transformation, though it reads more as a static flowchart than a true timeline.
